findings.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — `tempfile.size` stays stale after in-place resizing, causing all five reductions to run and `Upload.create_for` to receive the original size, so valid downsized uploads are rejected
app/models/optimized_image.rb:147 — The four-argument `downsize` definition replaces the existing width/height method because Ruby does not support overloading, breaking callers of the original API

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Passing `"80%"` to the animated-GIF downsizing path is invalid because `gifsicle --resize-fit` requires `WIDTHxHEIGHT`, preventing large animated GIFs from being downsized

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — The generic upload validator enforces a fixed 10 MB limit for every upload type instead of respecting `max_attachment_size_kb`, causing attachments to be transferred only to fail server-side or incorrectly blocked when the configured limit is higher

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify the same core issue: the code hardcodes a fixed 10MB (10 * 1024 KB) limit instead of using the configurable site settings like 'max_attachment_size_kb' or 'max_' + type + '_size_kb'. Both point out that this causes client-side limits to diverge from server-side/configured settings, leading to incorrect validation behavior.
